facts.statement: Khaan is an extinct oviraptorid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Mongolia.
facts.quote: Khaan (; from Mongol 'lord') is an extinct genus of oviraptorid dinosaur known from remains found in the Djadochta Formation of Mongolia, dating to the Late Cretaceous (Campanian, 75-71 million years ago).

facts.statement: Khaan was physically similar to other oviraptorid dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Khaan did not differ much from other oviraptorids.

facts.statement: Khaan was likely at least partially carnivorous, eating small vertebrates such as mammals, lizards, and possibly other small dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Like other oviraptorids, Khaan was probably at least partially a meat eater, feeding on small vertebrates like mammals, lizards and possibly other small dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Khaan was probably covered in feathers.
facts.quote: It was also probably feathered.

facts.statement: The main Khaan specimens found together were about four feet long.
facts.quote: These individuals are about four feet long.

facts.statement: A third specimen of Khaan, IGM 100/973, was considerably larger than the main specimens.
facts.quote: A third, considerably larger, specimen, IGM 100/973, was referred to the species.

facts.statement: The species Khaan mckennai was named by James M. Clark and colleagues in 2001.
facts.quote: The type species Khaan mckennai was named by James M. Clark et al. in 2001.

facts.statement: The specific name mckennai honors the paleontologist Malcolm Carnegie McKenna.
facts.quote: The specific name honours the paleontologist Malcolm Carnegie McKenna.

facts.statement: Khaan is classified within the family Oviraptoridae.
facts.quote: Khaan was by Clark assigned to the Oviraptoridae.

facts.statement: Among oviraptorids, Khaan was likely more closely related to Conchoraptor.
facts.quote: Among oviraptorids, it was probably more closely related to Conchoraptor.

facts.statement: Khaan lived approximately 72 million years ago during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 72 millones de años, en el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: Khaan was found in the Djadokhta Formation in Mongolia, with the holotype being an almost complete skeleton slightly disarticulated in the chest.
facts.quote: Khaan fue encontrado en la Formación Djadotcha en Mongolia, el holotipo es un esqueleto completo, desarticulado levemente en el tórax.

facts.statement: A 2014 study published in Nature suggests that Khaan may have been sexually dimorphic.
facts.quote: Según un estudio de 2014 publicado en Nature, Khaan posiblemente tenía dimorfismo sexual.

facts.statement: Researchers thought that reduced chevron spines were a female characteristic because they would provide more space for laying eggs.
facts.quote: Se pensaba que las espinas reducidas eran una característica femenina, porque aumentarían el espacio para poner huevos.

facts.statement: Larger chevron spines were hypothesized to be for male muscle attachments, potentially supporting a tail fan.
facts.quote: Además, las espinas más grandes podrían ser para accesorios musculares masculinos, lo que apoyaría un abanico de cola.

facts.statement: The species name was chosen to honor Dr. Malcolm McKenna.
facts.quote: La especie se nombra en honor al Dr. Malcolm McKenna.

facts.statement: Khaan was once tied with Minmi as the dinosaur genus with the shortest non-avian name until the discovery of Mei and later Yi qi.
facts.quote: Khaan, χaːŋ, es en mongol señor, estaba en igualdad con Minmi como el género no-aviar más corto nombre del dinosaurio, hasta la aparición de Mei y el posterior Yi qi.

facts.statement: The diet of oviraptorids like Khaan is debated, with suggestions ranging from plants to molluscs.
facts.quote: The oviraptorid diet is disputed, with plants and molluscs having been suggested.

facts.statement: A 2022 study suggests that Khaan possessed a very strong bite force compared to other oviraptorosaurs.
facts.quote: A 2022 study of the bite force of Khaan and comparisons with other oviraptorosaurs such as Incisivosaurus, Citipati, and Conchoraptor suggests that Khaan had a very strong bite force.

facts.statement: While moderate jaw gape usually indicates herbivory, Khaan likely fed on tougher vegetation than other herbivorous theropods like ornithomimosaurs and therizinosaurs.
facts.quote: The moderate jaw gape seen in oviraptorosaurs is indicative of herbivory in the majority of the group, but it is clear they were likely feeding on much tougher or more types of vegetation than other herbivorous theropods in their environment, such as ornithomimosaurs and therizinosaurs were able to.

facts.statement: Examinations suggest oviraptorosaurs may have been either powerful-biting generalists or specialists utilizing niche partitioning based on body size and cranial function.
facts.quote: The examinations suggest oviraptorosaurs may have been powerful-biting generalists or specialists that partook of niche partitioning both in body size and cranial function.

facts.statement: Khaan differs from Conchoraptor in several nasal region characteristics.
facts.quote: Khaan se diferencia de Conchoraptor en varias características de la región nasal.

facts.statement: The reduction of the third metacarpal is a distinctive feature of Khaan mckennai, unless the postcranium is not specialized.
facts.quote: La reducción próxima de su tercer metacarpiano es una característica distintiva de Khaan mckennai, si no el postcráneo no es especializado.

facts.statement: Khaan differs from Ajancingenia in that its first metacarpal is not extremely wide.
facts.quote: Se diferencia de Ajancingenia en que el primer metacarpiano no es extremadamente amplio.

facts.statement: The time range for Khaan is estimated from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)
